headline.purpose: The page title, one per screen.

body.purpose: Page-level descriptive prose, capped at max-w-prose.

body-sm.purpose: The console's working size: table cells, rows, buttons, inputs, help text. Most of the interface.

mono.purpose: Literal values read or copied exactly — flag keys, raw errors. Inherited from Tailwind defaults; should become a real token.

motion.name: transition-colors
motion.value: transition-property: color, background-color, border-color; transition-duration: 150ms; transition-timing-function: cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)
motion.purpose: The system's entire motion vocabulary, inherited from Tailwind's default. Colour moves; geometry never does. No duration or easing token is declared — adding one is a deliberate decision.

motion.name: focus-ring-no-transition
motion.purpose: Tailwind's transition-colors transitions outline-color, so without this the focus ring fades in over 150ms from each control's own currentColor. The indicator must be correct on the frame focus arrives.

gaps.note: No box-shadow exists anywhere. Flat is sufficient for the surfaces that exist, but there is no answer for a floating surface (dialog, popover, toast). Design it deliberately before the first one ships.
brand-accent, rounded-sm, rounded-lg and the entire spacing scale are generated but referenced by no component. Adopt deliberately or delete.

narrative.overview:
Atlas is built for someone who lives in it all day. Nothing here is composed to be admired; it is composed to be scanned. Rows are tight, separators are hairlines, and the eye travels down a list of fifty audit events without a single ornament to step over. The register is workmanlike on purpose — an administrator revoking access or flipping a rollout is mid-task, and the interface's job is to get out of the way while staying unambiguous about what is on, who did it, and what is broken.

The system earns its character from restraint rather than expression. Surfaces are flat. Type is the operating system's own. The entire palette is neutral slate until something has state — and then, and only then, colour arrives: indigo for the action you are meant to take or the route you are on, green/amber/red for a condition the system is reporting. Because colour is rationed this way, a single red badge in a sidebar is impossible to miss. That rationing is the design.

What this is not: a marketing surface. There is no hero, no gradient, no illustration, and no moment that exists to impress. The one concession to personality is a small set of emoji glyphs standing in as domain icons, which read as placeholders and are treated as such.
keyCharacteristics: Flat by construction — no shadow exists anywhere in the system.
Hairline 1px borders and a single surface-over-background tonal step carry all structure.
Neutral slate ground; colour is reserved for state and action.
Dense vertical rhythm — 0.5rem/0.75rem control padding, 1.5rem page padding.
Native system type, no webfont, no font loading cost.
Every semantic colour is defined twice, light and dark, and components read only the semantic name.
One focus ring for the whole system, in the text colour, offset so it never sits on a control own fill.
One drawn icon set, stroke-only at a single weight, always currentColor.

rules.name: The Rationed Colour Rule
rules.body: The interface is neutral until something has state. Control Indigo marks the action to take or the route you are on; a status hue marks a condition the system is reporting. If a colour is doing neither, it does not belong on the screen.

rules.name: The Two Borders Rule
rules.body: border separates content; border-strong bounds a control. They are not interchangeable and the distinction is load-bearing: a control outlined only in border fails WCAG 1.4.11, and an e2e suite measures exactly this. When a control’s resting outline is its only affordance, it uses border-strong.

rules.name: The Paired Ink Rule
rules.body: Every status tint has a dedicated on-* ink that inverts between themes — dark on the tint in light mode, light in dark mode. The status hue itself does not clear AA at label size on its own 15% tint (measured 3.65:1), so a tinted surface is never allowed to borrow the hue as its own text colour.

rules.name: The Semantic-Only Rule
rules.body: Components read bg, surface, text, text-muted, border, border-strong, on-*. They never read a light-* or dark-* token directly. The semantic alias is what makes one component correct in both themes, and reaching past it is how a dark-mode bug ships.

rules.name: The Working Size Rule
rules.body: The console's default is 0.875rem, not 1rem. Density is the point: a size bump reads as a demotion of everything around it, so a new component matches the working size unless it is a page title.

rules.name: The Literal Value Rule
rules.body: Monospace means "this string is exact" — a key, an identifier, an error as the system emitted it. It is never used for emphasis or flavour.

rules.name: The Uniform Page Padding Rule
rules.body: Every routed screen opens with p-6. The frame owns the chrome; the screen owns its content and nothing in between. A screen that sets its own outer padding breaks alignment with the module beside it in the nav, which is the one visual promise federation has to keep.

rules.name: The Header Row Rule
rules.body: A screen title and its status badges live on one wrapping flex row, title block left, badges right. It is how an operator finds "what is the state of this domain" in the same place on every screen, including screens owned by different teams in different repositories.

rules.name: The Tonal Step Rule
rules.body: A raised surface is lighter than its ground in both themes. Dark mode does not invert the relationship — dark-surface is lighter than dark-bg for the same reason light-surface is lighter than light-bg. Any new surface token keeps that direction or the structure stops being readable.

rules.name: The One Radius Rule
rules.body: Interactive and container surfaces are 0.5rem. Deviating needs a reason the shape itself communicates — as rounded-full does on a badge, where the pill form is what distinguishes a status from a button.

rules.name: The Colour on Movement Rule
rules.body: Hover and active states change colour. They do not move, scale, lift or shadow. transition-colors is the system’s entire motion vocabulary and there is no duration or easing token — adding one is a deliberate decision, not a component-level convenience.

rules.name: The Focus Ring Rule
rules.body: One ring, declared once, for everything: a 2px solid outline in the semantic text colour at outline-offset 2px, from libs/shared/ui/src/focus-visible.css, imported by all four apps and by Storybook. text rather than a focus token because text is by definition legible against anything the system paints, so the ring clears 3:1 against every surface that exists and any added later. The 2px offset is load-bearing: backgrounds paint only inside the border box, so the gap shows the parent background and never the control fill — without it the ring sits on the indigo and red fills at 2.84:1 and 3.70:1. And it must not animate: transition-colors includes outline-color, so the ring would otherwise fade in from each control currentColor. Never write outline: none.

rules.name: The Drawn Icon Rule
rules.body: Icons come from the shared set in libs/shared/ui/src/lib/icon: stroke-only on a 20px grid at a single 1.5 weight, round caps and joins, no fills, always currentColor. The manifest carries an icon NAME, not a glyph, so a domain icon is a registry edit like everything else about it (ADR-0004); an unrecognised name renders verbatim, because the manifest ships independently of the bundle and a deploy must never empty the nav. currentColor is what keeps an icon inside the Rationed Colour Rule rather than exempt from it — which is exactly what the emoji it replaced were not.

rules.name: The One Breakpoint Rule
rules.body: md (768px) is the only breakpoint in the system. A component that needs a second one is usually a component that should change shape once, not three times — and every extra breakpoint is another pair of layouts that has to stay correct in both themes.

rules.name: The Page Never Pans Rule
rules.body: Horizontal scrolling belongs to a container, never to the document. A table may overflow inside its own box; if the document scrolls sideways the chrome leaves with it, and the page is broken rather than dense.

rules.name: The Undo Over Confirm Rule
rules.body: A reversible action is acknowledged and offers Undo; it does not ask first. A confirm dialog interrupts every action to guard against the rare one, and an operator working down a list learns to dismiss it unread. Only an action that would remove the ability to undo it — losing your own access, or the platform last administrator — is refused outright, and a refusal always says why on the control itself.

rules.name: The Silent Success Rule
rules.body: No write completes without saying so. A label flipping is not feedback: it is invisible to a screen reader, and invisible to anyone whose eyes were on the control they clicked rather than on a counter at the far corner of the screen.

dos: Do read semantic colour tokens only — bg, surface, text, text-muted, border, border-strong, on-*. They are what make a component correct in both themes.
Do use border-strong for a control’s boundary and border for content separation. A control outlined only in border fails WCAG 1.4.11 and an e2e suite measures it.
Do pair every status tint with its on-* ink.
Do edit libs/shared/design-tokens/tokens/*.json to change a token, then regenerate. The committed CSS is generated and tokens:check fails on drift — hand-editing it is a gate failure, not a shortcut.
Do keep p-6 on every routed screen and the title-left / badges-right header row. Cross-remote alignment is federation’s one visual promise.
Do default to the 0.875rem working size and 0.5rem radius.
Do prefer aria-busy to disabled for an action just triggered.
Do put anything a second surface needs into libs/shared/ui. Drift between independently deployed remotes is this architecture’s defining failure mode.
Do verify both themes for every change. A component that passes light and fails dark fails.
Do leave focus to the shared ring. It already covers <button>, <a>, <input>, [tabindex] holders and anything added later.
Do draw a new icon into the shared set at the same 1.5 stroke weight on the 20px grid, in currentColor, and give the manifest its name.
Do let a dense table scroll inside its own container at phone width, and never let the document pan.
Do acknowledge every write in the screen action status, and offer Undo unless the action is one of the refusals.
donts: Don’t add a box-shadow to a single component. The system has no elevation vocabulary; an improvised value becomes the de facto system without anyone choosing it. Design it deliberately, once.
Don’t introduce a webfont. Native system type is a committed decision.
Don’t reach past a semantic token to a light-* or dark-* value.
Don’t spend Control Indigo on anything that is not the primary action or the active route. Its rarity is what makes it readable.
Don’t use a status hue as text on its own tint, or a status colour to set a mood.
Don’t animate geometry. Colour transitions only — no transform, lift or scale.
Don’t make a badge interactive, or give a button a pill radius. The shapes are how an operator tells a report from a control.
Don’t remove or disable the navigation item for a failed remote. It is the route back in.

Don’t adopt brand-accent, rounded-sm, rounded-lg or the spacing scale by accident. They are declared but unconsumed; adopting one is a system decision, and the honest alternatives are adopt deliberately or delete.
Don't write outline: none, anywhere, for any reason. It is the single edit that can remove focus indication outright.
Don't add a focus utility to a component. The shared ring covers it; a local one would fragment the only indicator a keyboard user has.
Don't let outline-color transition. transition-colors includes it, and an indicator that fades in is not an indicator on the frame it is needed.
Don't reach for an emoji, a Unicode glyph, or an icon font. The set is drawn; a glyph is a different weight, a different colour, and a different shape on every operating system.
Don't give an icon its own colour. currentColor is what keeps it inside the colour ration.
Don't add a second breakpoint. md is the whole vocabulary: the console is either at a desk or in a hand.
Don't add a confirmation dialog to a reversible action.
Don't let a write complete silently, or signal it only by a control changing.
